articles.topic: Amino acid arginine supports immune function
articles.headline: Arginine Might Be the Immune Tool You're Missing
articles.body: Arginine, an amino acid found in protein-rich foods, plays a surprisingly important role in helping your immune system spot cancer and viral infections. Recent research from Rockefeller University shows that arginine deficiency may weaken your immune response. The body produces arginine naturally, and you get it from foods like chicken, beef, and fish. If your arginine is running low, your immune cells can't do their job as effectively. This isn't about megadosing—it's about making sure you're hitting baseline levels through diet or targeted supplementation.
articles.takeaway: Ensure adequate arginine intake through protein-rich foods or supplementation to support your immune system's ability to fight infections and stay resilient.

articles.topic: Cognitive training improves brain health at any age
articles.headline: Your Brain Doesn't Stop Getting Smarter. Here's the Proof
articles.body: A three-year study of nearly 4,000 adults aged 19 to 94 shows your cognitive abilities can improve at any stage of life. Participants spent just five to 15 minutes daily on brain training activities using the BrainHealth Index, which measures clarity, connectedness, and emotional balance. The results? Sustained improvements across the board, regardless of baseline scores. Higher engagement with training tools—especially strategy-based learning and coaching—produced the greatest gains. This challenges the narrative that mental decline is inevitable and shows you have real agency over your brain health.
articles.takeaway: Dedicate 5-15 minutes daily to cognitive training. Consistency and active engagement drive measurable improvements in brain health at any age.

articles.topic: Weekend sleep recovery reduces teen depression risk
articles.headline: Sleeping In on Weekends Actually Protects Your Mental Health
articles.body: Teens who made up for lost weekday sleep by sleeping in on weekends had a significantly lower risk of depression, according to recent research. Your sleep debt isn't just about feeling tired—it directly impacts your mental health. When you're chronically sleep-deprived during the week, recovery sleep on weekends matters. The key insight: while consistent sleep schedules are ideal, allowing yourself to catch up on lost sleep provides real psychological protection. For busy adults juggling work and family, this is permission to prioritize those weekend hours of rest.
articles.takeaway: If you can't get consistent weekday sleep, prioritize recovery sleep on weekends. Catching up on lost sleep has measurable mental health benefits.

articles.topic: Cold water immersion beats cryotherapy for muscle soreness
articles.headline: Cold Plunge Wins. Here's Why Cryotherapy Chambers Lost
articles.body: A 2026 meta-analysis comparing cold water immersion and whole-body cryotherapy found that dunking in cold water produced significantly greater reduction in muscle soreness at the 24-hour mark. The difference was meaningful and consistent across studies. At 48 hours, the advantage faded, but the acute recovery benefit of cold water was clear. The takeaway for you: if you're choosing between an expensive cryotherapy session and a cold plunge or ice bath, water immersion is the more efficient tool for managing post-workout soreness. Cost matters, and cold water works.
articles.takeaway: Cold water immersion is more effective than whole-body cryotherapy for reducing muscle soreness in the 24 hours after training.

workout.title: Pull Strong: Row, Hang and Brace in 30
workout.tip: If you don't have a pull-up bar, a sturdy door frame pull-up bar works fine. For the dead hang, focus on active shoulders, squeeze your shoulder blades down before you hang. That protects your joints and builds the right muscles.
workout.warmup: Spend 3 minutes loosening up your upper body: 10 arm circles each direction, 10 band pull-aparts or towel pull-aparts, and 30 seconds of hanging from the bar in a passive dead hang to open up the lats and shoulders.

exercises.name: Dead Hang
exercises.notes: Grip the bar with both hands shoulder-width apart. Let your shoulders pack down and back, not shrug up to your ears. Build grip and shoulder stability. Rest 60 seconds between sets.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bent-Over Row
exercises.notes: Hinge at the hips to about 45 degrees, keep your lower back flat. Drive the elbow straight back and squeeze at the top. Avoid rotating your torso. Go heavier than feels comfortable.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Face Pull
exercises.notes: Anchor the band at face height. Pull the band toward your nose, driving elbows out wide and up. Pause briefly at the end range. This is the most underrated shoulder health exercise you aren't doing enough.

exercises.name: Inverted Row (or Assisted Pull-Up with Band)
exercises.notes: For inverted row: use a table edge or low bar, heels on the floor, body in a plank. Pull your chest to the bar. For band-assisted pull-up: loop band on bar, place one knee in band, pull chin over bar. Both count.

exercises.name: Plank to Alternating Shoulder Tap
exercises.notes: Keep your hips square and still as you lift each hand off the floor to tap the opposite shoulder. Slow and controlled beats fast and sloppy every time. Great anti-rotation core work.

workout.cooldown: Finish with 60 seconds of passive hanging from the bar to decompress the spine, followed by a 60-second doorway chest and shoulder stretch to rebalance after all the pulling.

meal.title: Cottage Cheese & Pepperoni Bowl
meal.description: High-protein dairy paired with savory cured meat and whole grain crackers creates a satisfying strength snack that mimics a charcuterie board. Cottage cheese delivers casein protein for sustained muscle amino acid availability.
meal.instructions:
1. Scoop cottage cheese into a small bowl.
2. Top with pepperoni slices and a grind of black pepper.
3. Serve with crackers on the side for scooping, or crumble crackers into the cottage cheese for texture.
meal.tip: Buy cottage cheese in bulk on Sunday and pre-portion into 150g containers for grab-and-go snacking all week. Pairs perfectly with a cup of coffee as an afternoon pick-me-up.
